status: Seven-code coherent global natural-disaster/response inquiry through existing research, argument-evidence, writing and map claims. No new inquiry/topic/event clone.

completeClaims: FW9: three learner-formulated research questions, two sources for each, brief organised print notes and a two-source written synthesis.
How authors support points: identify points/reasons/evidence, judge relevance and sufficiency and separate supported claims from unsupported assertions.
Evidence-based writing: cited factual analysis, accurate two-source synthesis noting agreement/difference, paraphrase and source list.
Reading/drawing maps: retain actual familiar-space map/key/labels/relative landmarks separately; a world-map overlay alone does not certify that whole claim.
Coordinates: retain complete paired reference/read+plot/hemisphere+zero/actual approximation/changed-view tasks, not just look up a country.
claimReview.closestExcluded: Judging reliable information has explicit health-professional/social-media/own-health-choice evidence; it is not relabelled as generic policy evaluation. Scientific pattern/conclusion inventories are not added merely to make charts from arbitrary aid counts.
claimReview.readiness: Whole Shared Research, Author Purpose, Main Topic/Paragraph Detail and familiar-plan hard prerequisites remain unchanged and unassumed. No forced prerequisite association, automatic mastery or source-specific age lowering.

needs-response.question: What urgent needs and international connections followed the 2010 Haiti earthquake, and how did Canadian-government and Red Cross responses address them?
sources: Canadian Red Cross Haiti historical/partnership account
needs-response.limits: The current NGO account includes later work; distinguish the paragraph about 2010 from later projects. Do not present donor accounts as every Haitian resident’s perspective.

giving-matching.question: How did individual giving connect with the government matching scheme, and what do the reported February 2010 figures establish or leave unknown?
giving-matching.limits: Both are Canadian-government documents, not independent corroboration. Potential eligibility, actual matching and delivered outcome are different.

different-response-needs.question: How were responses adapted to particular physical/health/access needs in Haiti 2010 and Nepal 2015, and what evidence supports a conclusion about cooperation and effectiveness?
different-response-needs.limits: Different locations, periods and institutional perspectives; no rank based on unlike output units or an assumption Canada led all local action.

preparedData.period: Reported as of 12 February 2010 in the 22 February 2010 statement
preparedData.measure: Money raised by the 14 major Canadian NGOs referenced in that report
interpretationLimits: The second row is a subset of the first, not an additional separate contribution; do not add them.
Potentially eligible is not confirmed matched or money delivered to every recipient.
The separate Chelsea student figure of 2000 CAD is an individual-group example, not another total for the same 14 organizations or a common millions unit.

preparation: Adult setup: provide original attributed fact summaries and sufficiently substantial multi-paragraph excerpts from the actual government/NGO accounts in print and digital form, plus the original map assets. Exclude unviewed imagery/films and unrelated site content.

Keep dates, authors/institutions, purposes and evidence locators attached. Prepare a notes template with question/source/fact/claim/limit headings, the exact-unit data table, country/city reference maps and a blank labelled flow-map base.

For full familiar-map knowledge, retain an actual own-classroom/school/park reading/drawing check with key, labels, relative landmarks and route, distinct from the additional international application. No private home address is collected.
actions: Formulate three research questions covering issue/impact/responses and a comparison/evaluation, using the actual models as supports rather than the adult answering for the learner. Identify and actually use at least two suitable sources for EACH question.

Gather information using print reading/notes and digital article/map tools. Take brief notes from a print source, sort them under meaningful headings, and record which source supports or limits each finding. Do not treat one source copied on two websites as independent evidence.

Analyse the political country reference and local graticule/city map in print and digital form: locate Canada and affected Haiti/Port-au-Prince, retain the source-rounded position and distinguish a city locator from an earthquake epicentre or delivery address. Use the prior full coordinate contrasts/transfer as the whole-claim check.

Construct an actual print thematic map of the affected place and relevant Canadian connections, and a digital flow map of supported funding/organizational cooperation, using a verified country base, title, key, labels and source/date. Arrows represent supported relationships, not invented flight routes or exact aid distribution. Explain each map’s contribution to at least one question. The original country map may be zoomed/referenced; additional locations must be checked against the actual publisher reference.

Interpret the actual table with its currency/unit/date/subset qualifiers. Use a comparison organizer for needs/actors/actions in the separate disasters and an evidence-to-claim table; these tools answer the selected questions. No chart of source mentions or mixed-unit output totals is manufactured.

Identify actual key claims in at least two informational accounts and the particular facts/examples offered. Judge relevant/sufficient support, distinguish an achieved reported action from a promise or unsupported total-recovery claim, and explain institutional purpose/perspective without calling all official or NGO accounts either infallible or worthless.

Draw conclusions answering the three questions about international impacts/responses and cooperation, with an explicit criterion for any effectiveness judgment. Carry the actual selected question/category through notes, relevant map/evidence and conclusions; record a justified remaining uncertainty rather than fill it with invented testimony.

Write an original short report/summary that synthesizes at least two informational sources, notes agreement/difference, cites actual facts/locators and paraphrases accurately; present findings orally with the print/digital maps and table. Use terms such as NGO, aid, response, cooperation, evidence and matching accurately, not as a full unrelated vocabulary inventory.
requiredWholeClaimChecks: Three actual questions and two sources per question; organised print notes.
Written two-source synthesis and cited/paraphrased analysis with agreement/difference.
Both print and digital analysis AND construction; different map types and their meaningful inquiry roles, plus complete retained map/coordinate checks.
Information AND actual numerical data, with source/date/unit/subset limits, and evidence-based conclusions about impacts/responses.
nearMisses: Adult supplies three headings but learner never formulates/questions or uses a second source for each.
Copies a source or says all donated money was confirmed matched/delivered.
Only views a digital map, or adds arrows/charts with no bearing on the question.
Uses an official source as proof of every outcome without evaluating the actual evidence.

whole-inquiry.operation: Carry out the complete coherent inquiryProtocol: issue, global impacts, responses, relevant maps/data/evidence and actual communication, not a link-count rollup.

questions.operation: Formulate and use the three actual inquiry questions with the described issue/impact/response/comparison scope and two suitable sources for each.

gathering.operation: Gather and organise actual print/digital text, numerical information and spatial resources using notes and map/article tools; preserve source/date/purpose and local-partner limits.

maps.operation: Complete the actual print AND digital analysis AND construction of different meaningful map types in inquiryProtocol, keeping whole familiar-map and coordinate operations explicit and separate from the global application.

analysis.operation: Interpret and analyse actual numerical table, maps and qualitative source information with the relevant organizers and evidence-to-claim comparisons, retaining units/subset/date and relevance/sufficiency limits.

conclusions.operation: Evaluate actual support and draw original question-linked conclusions about global impacts/responses and effectiveness, distinguishing supported results, perspective and remaining uncertainty.

communication.operation: Produce the actual original cited two-source report/synthesis and oral/map/data presentation, using relevant terms and formats and noting agreement/difference without plagiarism.

coverageBoundary: Source-fit authoring programme, not completed pupil work, every source’s independent truth, all humanitarian outcomes or a whole-Ontario completion claim. Actual print/digital products are task requirements; this does not fabricate classroom observations.
